chunk_findings.detail: The conflict notice is built from the user-supplied `target` string, not the resolved `peer` ref. For a repository whose default branch is `master`, `ddflow probe A` (no `--against`) resolves `peer = W.default_branch(repo)` to `master`, but `_text(res, item, target)` returns “Merge main into the branch” and the recorded event stores `against: "main"`. If there is no `main` branch, the instructed next action names a ref that cannot be merged. The same defect appears for `--against PEER_ID`: the message tells the user to merge the item id rather than the peer’s actual branch, and the only next command shown is bare `ddflow wait` with no MCP form. This violates the project’s tell-dont-discover requirement that refusals/notices name the exact next call/ref in CLI and MCP form [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/probe.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `p.method == PR.MERGE_TREE` even though the probe is specified to check the git version and fall back to a scratch merge when `merge-tree` is unusable (the intent explicitly names git 2.43 returning 129). On a supported git 2.43 environment, `PR.run` should return `PR.CLEAN` with `PR.SCRATCH`, so the assertion at line 57 fails even though the probe behaved correctly. The test should either force a merge-tree-capable version via `git_version` or assert only that the result is clean.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_conflict_probe.py:test_clean_pair

chunk_findings.detail: This test monkeypatches `PR.G.run` to return an unavailable result only for `merge-tree`, but it does not force the probe to take the merge-tree path. On an environment where the real git version is old enough that the probe skips merge-tree and uses the scratch merge (again, git 2.43 is explicitly called out), `PR.run` never invokes the monkeypatched `merge-tree` call, performs a clean scratch merge, and returns `PR.CLEAN`; the assertion at line 104 then fails. The test should monkeypatch `git_version` to a merge-tree-capable version, or otherwise skip when merge-tree is not used.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_conflict_probe.py:test_a_timeout_is_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: `tip()` treats every non-zero `G.run` result as “ref does not exist” by returning `""` whenever `r.ok` is false. If `G.run` is unavailable because git is missing, the probe timeout expired, or a git lock is held, `run()` then takes the `if not sha` branch and returns `UNAVAILABLE` with reason `'<ref>' is not a commit of this repository`. Given a timeout on `git rev-parse --verify`, the result says the ref is missing instead of timeout/git-unavailable, and the later “git could not be run” path is bypassed, so the probe records the wrong failure reason and can point the operator to the wrong next call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/probe.py:tip/run

chunk_findings.detail: The scratch fallback recovers conflict paths by searching `str(why)` with `_FILES = re.compile(r"conflicting files: ([^;]*)")` and then splitting the captured text on commas and stripping each item. Git filenames may contain commas, semicolons, and leading/trailing spaces. A single conflicting path `a,b.txt` is parsed as two paths `('a', 'b.txt')`, and a path `a;b.txt` is truncated at the semicolon, so the fallback probe records incorrect conflicting paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/probe.py:_scratch/_FILES

chunk_findings.detail: `data` is built with a `text` key, then line 75 calls `O.failed(KIND, data["text"], **data)` and line 77 calls `O.nothing(KIND, data["text"], **data)`. Because `**data` also contains `text`, the conflict and unavailable paths pass `text` twice — once positionally and once by keyword — so a probe that returns `CONFLICT` or `UNAVAILABLE` raises `TypeError: ... got multiple values for argument 'text'` after the event has already been appended, instead of returning the documented exit-1/exit-2 outcome.

chunk_findings.detail: The item lookup `if target in st.items:` is performed before the `main` special case, so an item whose id is literally `main` hijacks the default-branch probe. For example, with repository default branch `trunk` and an item id `main` whose branch is `feature/main`, `ddflow probe ITEM` with no `--against` (or `--against main`) should probe against `trunk`, but line 51 sets `peer` to `feature/main`, line 61 records/reports `feature/main` as the probe target, and the probe answer is against the wrong ref.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/probe.py:50

chunk_findings.detail: The conflict refusal text names only the CLI form `ddflow wait` and a manual merge instruction; it does not name the exact next call in MCP form, unlike the unavailable path which includes `ddflow_probe`. This violates the change’s conformance requirement that every refusal/notice name the exact next call in CLI and MCP form [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/probe.py:37

chunk_findings.detail: `_probe_at` silently treats any non-list/tuple value as an empty list with no reported problem: `items = list(value) if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) else []`. If `probe_at` is supplied as a scalar string through one of the supported configuration paths, e.g. `DDFLOW_LOCKS_PROBE_AT=claim` or an MCP/config call that passes `"claim"` instead of `["claim"]`, the function returns `([], [])`. The knob loader therefore accepts the setting, reports no problem, and stores an empty `probe_at`, so automatic probes at claim/gate/merge are disabled even though the user asked for them. This makes the list knob not reliably settable in its intended four ways and can silently turn off probing. [r-everything-configurable]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/locks.py:_probe_at

chunk_findings.detail: In the scratch-merge fallback, `_scratch` reconstructs conflicting paths by regex-capturing everything after `conflicting files:` up to a semicolon and then splitting on commas and stripping whitespace. Git paths may legally contain commas, semicolons, and leading/trailing spaces, and the captured segment can also be empty. For a conflict on the single file `a,b`, a CI conflict reason like `conflicting files: a,b;` makes `_FILES.group(1)` be `a,b`, `split(",")` yields two names, and the Probe records paths `('a', 'b')` instead of `('a,b',)`; a reason like `conflicting files: ;` records an invalid empty path. These wrong paths are then propagated to probe events and notices.

chunk_findings.detail: The test simulates a merge-tree timeout by monkeypatching only `PR.G.run` for the `merge-tree` command, but it does not force `PR.git_version` to report a modern git. The file’s own `test_old_git_falls_back_to_a_scratch_merge` shows that `PR.run` checks `git_version` and chooses `SCRATCH` before calling `merge-tree` on old git. Therefore, on a supported old-git environment (e.g. git 2.30), `PR.run(pair, "ddflow/clean", "main", timeout_s=1)` never invokes the monkeypatched `merge-tree`; it runs the scratch merge on the clean pair and returns `PR.CLEAN`, so the assertion that the result is `PR.UNAVAILABLE` fails. The test should pin `PR.git_version` to a modern tuple or skip the merge-tree-specific timeout test when real git lacks usable merge-tree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_conflict_probe.py:test_a_timeout_is_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: The test helper bypasses the git adapter and invokes git directly with `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`. The change’s conformance and [r-adapters] require git to be reached only through `infra.git`; this raw subprocess path avoids the adapter’s handling of environment, timeouts, and unavailable status, violating the one-port rule. Use `ddflow.infra.git`/`PR.G.run` (or a dedicated test adapter) for git setup instead.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_conflict_probe.py:14 `_git`

chunk_findings.detail: In `probe`, the conflict path returns `O.failed(KIND, data["text"], **data)`, and the unavailable path at the next return does the same with `O.nothing(KIND, data["text"], **data)`. `data` already contains the key `"text"` (`"text": _text(res, item, shown)`), so when the outcome constructors take `text` as their second positional parameter — as the nearby `O.ok(KIND, **data)` path relies on — this passes `text` twice and raises `TypeError: got multiple values for argument 'text'`. Any conflicting pair, or `[locks].probe` off / probe unavailable, therefore crashes instead of returning the documented conflict or unavailable outcome.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/probe.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: `shown = peer if target == MAIN else target  # the ref actually probed` is wrong when `--against` names another item whose lease branch differs from its item id. `peer = _branch(st, cfg, target)` resolves the branch actually passed to `PR.run`, but `shown` is reset to the item id. For example, peer item `ddflow-43` with lease branch `users/bob/topic` is probed against `users/bob/topic`, but the returned data has `"against": "ddflow-43"` and the conflict text says `Merge ddflow-43 into the branch`, which is not a git ref. The event consumer cannot recover the actual peer branch from `against`; it only has the peer sha in `base`.

chunk_findings.detail: The version parser only keeps major and minor components, so a patch-level minimum is ignored. With `min_git="2.38.1"` and a repository using git 2.38.0, `_tuple(min_git)` is `(2,38)` and `have < (2,38)` is false, so `run` uses `git merge-tree` instead of the documented scratch-merge fallback even though the configured minimum is not satisfied.

chunk_findings.detail: In scratch-merge conflict reporting, the code parses `why` with `_FILES` and `found.group(1).split(",")`. Comma is a valid byte in a git path, so a file named `a,b.txt` is reported as two conflict paths (`a` and `b.txt`) rather than one. The same `_FILES` regex also stops at `;`, truncating a path like `a;b.txt`. The structured conflict object should be used instead of string-splitting on delimiters that can appear in filenames.

chunk_findings.detail: The command documents exit statuses in `summary`/`description` (0 clean, 1 conflict, 2 unavailable), but the declaration contains no exit-code/status mapping: it only sets `cli=CliPolicy(body_always=True)`, and `conflict`/`unavailable` are returned in `payload` as normal results rather than raised errors. Given a conflicting pair, `ddflow probe ITEM --against PEER` will print the conflicting paths and exit 0, so any script relying on the documented exit status 0=clean will treat a conflict as merge-ready, violating the command's own “never read as clean” guarantee.

chunk_findings.detail: The test reaches git directly via `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], ...)` in `_git`, and other tests monkeypatch `PR.G.run` to simulate git results. chunk_findings.detail: The new conflict message tells the caller to repeat the probe with `ddflow probe {item} --against {against}`, where `against` is the `shown` value. When the request used the magic default-branch target, `shown` is the resolved default-branch name, not the literal `main` that was accepted as input. Because `probe()` resolves `--against` by first checking `target == MAIN` and then `target in st.items`, a default-branch name that is also an item id does not round-trip. Example: repository default branch is `trunk`, and there is an item id `trunk` whose lease branch is `users/alice/trunk`. `ddflow probe ddflow-1` (or `ddflow probe ddflow-1 --against main`) correctly probes against default branch `trunk` and reports a conflict. The returned text then says to re-probe with `ddflow probe ddflow-1 --against trunk`; running that command takes the `trunk in st.items` branch and probes `users/alice/trunk` instead, so an agent or script can see a clean re-probe while the conflict against default branch `trunk` remains. The earlier item-named-`main` fix does not answer this because it only special-cases the literal argument `main`; it does not make the resolved default-branch name safe to pass back through `--against` [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/probe.py:_text (conflict re-probe clause)

chunk_findings.detail: The new conflict-path filter `names = tuple(n for n in _both_changed(repo, item, against) if n in said)` treats any raw path that is a substring of the conflict prose as a conflicting path. Given a base containing files `a` and `a,b`, where the item and peer both modify `a` in non-overlapping hunks (so `a` merges cleanly) and both modify `a,b` in the same hunk (so only `a,b` conflicts), `_both_changed` returns both `a` and `a,b`; if `str(why)` contains `conflicting files: a,b;`, the substring test also matches `a`, so the Probe returns `a` as a conflicting path even though it was not conflicted. The fallback should restrict names to the actual conflicted path list, not arbitrary substring membership in the whole `why` text.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/probe.py:_scratch
